articles.body: As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow American approach to mediation. For Russia expert Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. "The Russian approach is always to sound incredibly bullish and then make any concessions at the very last minute," he explains, suggesting that the Kremlin's uncompromising rhetoric should not necessarily be mistaken for an absolute refusal to negotiate. Yet the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to surrender territory it continues to hold. "That Donbas question is, for me, an intractable one," Galeotti observes, warning that neither side currently appears willing to cede territory necessary for a breakthrough. Whereas conventional diplomacy generally proceeds through discreet negotiations before culminating in political announcements, Trump's approach has effectively reversed that sequence. "Trump makes grand declarations and various people try desperately to make it happen."

articles.body: You know you’ve made a good ad when it’s outperforming an endorsement video from Barack Obama. Ryan Sayles, a 27-year-old Mississippi content creator, is behind arguably the best political spot of the election cycle: Democrat Scott Colom’s viral “ pick another protein ” ad against GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. You’ve probably seen it by now. The ad featured Mississippi voters’ blunt reactions to Hyde-Smith’s suggestion that people struggling with rising beef prices choose from other protein options. “Pick another protein? Shiiii-, I’d rather pick another senator instead.” “Pick another protein? She done lost her damn mind. I’d rather pick another senator.” Sayles was at his nephew’s football game when he realized something extraordinary was happening. “I was looking at the first numbers when it first dropped, and I was like, ‘Oh, this is about to be a really good video,’” he told POLITICO after Colom’s historic Senate race victory in the longtime Republican stronghold. “We had the Obama endorsement the day before, so that was our biggest video. It was like, ‘Dang, we ain’t ever gonna top that.’” “And then this ad came, and we posted it, and it outperformed anything we ever did,” Sayles said. The 30-second spot quickly became the talk of Mississippi and Washington, helping fuel Colom’s longshot campaign to unseat Hyde-Smith and become the first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction. And, it’s given Democrats across the country another blueprint for how to break through online ahead of a critical 2028 presidential race, as the party continues to rethink its strategy. With the ad — and Colom’s win — Sayles has gone from a newcomer who stumbled into campaigning almost by accident to a name to watch in Democratic digital politics, as the party looks for fresh ways to reach voters ahead of 2028. “[Sayles] should be considered the breakout-star of this cycle,” Colom wrote in a post on X about the viral ad earlier this month. “He’s going to be a giant in the media consultant game. He did GAME CHANGING work with SO little.” In an interview with POLITICO, Sayles described how his lack of prior political experience shaped his approach to creating the ad and why he thinks Democrats should listen more closely to the voters they’re trying to reach. He also discussed the unexpected attention he’s received since the ad — and why he hopes Colom’s victory will serve as a wake-up call for the party to invest in the South. This interview has been edited for length and clarity.  How did you get involved with the Colom campaign?  I did a lot of freelance videography and photography, and they really just needed a photographer for one event they were doing back in October. And I came and did video and pictures for him, and they kept me around. They were like, "Yeah, we need to work with him,” and then from then on, I never left. Take me behind the scenes of creating the protein ad. How did it come together?  Scott and his brother, Andrew, along with [the] campaign manager Gerard, they all plotted the script together, and so they presented it to me. We filmed it, and I directed and made sure it [felt] like Mississippi. I guess I made it more Mississippi than what it was at the beginning. You know, [I] just added the entertainment or funny pieces of it, like emphasizing the way he said the words and stuff like that. And then I shot it, edited it, and added the music to it. I sat there and edited for like five hours. I've heard that man say “shit” a million times. Did you think it was going to go this viral?  I had high hopes for it, but I just didn't know what it could do. A lot of our content was getting around Mississippi, but it wasn't getting around the country. Mississippians knew about Scott Colom’s content and what he was doing, but it wasn't nationwide — and I think that ad really put a national focus on what was brewing in Mississippi. Why do you think this particular ad took off so much and felt so natural?  I think the reason it did well nationally is because I think a lot of people are fed up. A lot of times we don't express the way we feel, we hold it in, but I think this ad was an expression that people felt all around the country, that we just had the guts to put it out there. For Mississippi, of course it resonated because that's something we say down here. People say “shiiiit” all the time — like you know, that's the normal conversation. I think the best thing about the ad was it was centering people, centering voters ... You know, Scott was in the ad for about five seconds, but then that was the biggest ad of the cycle. I think it was just a lesson that people matter way more than politics. Did anybody worry the ad went too far? Do you think Democrats are sometimes too cautious?  I think the dope part is, we didn't run that ad by anybody. … We didn’t go around getting OK’s from anybody ... we just put it out. But also … I've never worked on a campaign, and I think that I didn't have a sense of what Dems normally did. You know what I mean? We just did what we liked, and that was one of the big things Scott always talked about. “Man, if we are good with the content, we are good.” Scott is the best person I could’ve been in this situation with. He has been such a great person. He’s so creative, and he has allowed me to shine in ways that I just can’t believe. Did you hear from people in the Democratic Party after the ad came out? Like I said, this is my first campaign, so this is all a blur right now, honestly. But I would say that I've gotten messages, a lot of messages. I don't know who all those messages are tied to at this point, but I have gotten a lot of messages and people saying, “You did great work, we should talk.” I'm just happy. Mississippi is, we have hope again, man, that's the biggest thing. You know, this is my state. What could the Democratic Party learn from the Colom campaign’s digital strategy?  I want to shout out my digital director. Lacy Nelson was the digital director, and she really helped turn things around when it came to just our distribution being able to put stuff out, because at first I was posting, taking pictures, filming, editing, doing everything by myself, and it was the worst headache. You gotta put your feet on the ground, you gotta understand the area in which you are working to try to get voters, and you gotta let them know that you see them and make them feel seen. You have to understand what resonates with people. People in Mississippi are not going to care about the things that somebody who lives in New York City cares about, it's going to be different. And that messaging needs to be different. You can't give Mississippi a New York message. Not that I'm an expert — like I said, this is my first campaign — but I think people should really focus on what that region is listening to. What does Colom’s victory mean for Democrats’ opportunities across the South?  For a long time we’ve looked at it as impossible. And with very little resources, we showed that if you really get out and you do the work, you talk to people, you meet voters where they are, it is possible. Mississippi is one of the hardest places that could have happened. When you look at the investment and you look at what other places have received for that type of thing, it shows that the opportunity was always in Mississippi. … We just needed the investment, and I think that over the years, so many organizations have done the work to get us to this point, and we just seized the opportunity. There's real opportunity in the South. You just gotta invest.
articles.headline: Meet the 27-year old behind the protein ad that helped flip Mississippi

articles.body: Democrats’ midterms sweep didn’t solve their ideological civil war — but a number of the party’s potential presidential contenders hope it lets them call a truce. In the days since Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories, several likely White House aspirants have argued that their party’s factional feuding needs to take a backseat heading into 2028. “What was clear, no matter where you go, [is that] people are frustrated,” Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro told reporters last weekend at Crooked Media’s post-election conference. “They're not thinking about whether this is about left or middle or right. They're thinking about how to get problems solved.” “I don't know if the takeaway should be what ideology that people wanted. I think people want results,” Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said at the same event. Democrats’ midterm tidal wave was powered more by voters’ anger at high costs and the Trump administration than by any one ideology. Candidates won tough races by positioning themselves not as progressives or moderates but as anti-Washington populists and pragmatists — some of them even scoring dual endorsements from both the moderate Blue Dog Democrats and progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.). “If you see … an elected leader spending valuable time duking it out on whose team won, moderate or progressive, they are missing the actual message of this election,” Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, a moderate who campaigned hard for progressive Abdul El-Sayed, told POLITICO. “It’s about people who are wanting to work together as a team on issues like the American dream in the middle class.”Many of the party’s rising stars embraced an ethos like Shapiro’s “get stuff done” and, like Slotkin, called to reject progressive-versus-moderate politics in favor of combative candidates. “It helps take away the most annoying question that has split our party, and that is the question of electability,” progressive Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said in an interview last week. “It turns out that progressives were electable, and centrists were electable. The moderates were electable, and people who were affiliated with the DSA were electable.” Now, as they pivot into 2028, Democrats are broadly seizing on last week’s results as license to avoid traditional labels as they look to appeal as widely as possible to voters more interested in easing the pinch in their pocketbooks than the political philosophy to which their leaders subscribe. Interviews and conversations with more than a dozen potential Democratic presidential candidates, advisers and operatives reveal that rhetorical shift is as much a rejection of the ideological litmus tests that dominated the 2020 primary as it is a calibration toward the dynamics that will drive the 2028 contest. “We all lived through the purity tests,” said Adrienne Elrod, a Democratic strategist who advised Joe Biden in 2020, Kamala Harris in 2024 and Hillary Clinton’s 2016 run. “What people are now yearning for is authenticity. And they want a fighter and someone who can deliver more than someone who perfectly aligns with them ideologically.” There are tells in the flurry of postelection memos from potential presidential contenders. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s team positioned her not as a progressive firebrand but as “one of the most effective voices in the country for America’s working class.” Teams behind Moore and Shapiro pushed messages of “common-sense governance” and “delivering results.” “There has been a reckoning in the Democratic Party, and people in all lanes frankly have come to realize the government in Washington has not delivered for working-class people and they need to,” said Jeff Weaver, a Khanna adviser who managed Sanders’ 2016 presidential campaign. Or, as one adviser to a potential candidate said: Voters “do not live in the binaries that a lot of political operatives do.” While last Tuesday’s wave swept Democrats of all stripes into office, it also created openings for each wing of the party to argue that its vision is the way forward. That all but guarantees more proxy battles to come as the party moves from running a raft of candidates across diverse districts to selecting just one to try and win the White House. The left has seized on strong performances by unabashedly progressive candidates to push Khanna and Ocasio-Cortez to run for president and Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. Ravi Mangla, a spokesperson for the Working Families Party, said it’s “undeniable the populist candidates … can win in swing states that are going to be critical in 2028” — and the left lane is “wide open.” But the centrist group Welcome argued in a new memo shared first with POLITICO that there’s a clear pathway for candidates willing to embrace a more moderate posture. “In a very large field, you need a base to get you to 15, 20, 25 percent. And it’s very clear in the data you can get there with voters in the middle — center-left voters,” said Welcome co-founder Liam Kerr. And even as he called for a primary that would battle test a diverse set of ideological views, Khanna, who co-chaired Sanders’ 2020 campaign, leaned into his liberal bona fides: “It would be an honor to be called a Bernie Sanders Democrat; I embrace being a New Deal Democrat with pride.” “Obviously, I'm a progressive Democrat. I believe that the progressive vision is the best vision. But there should be someone who’s in the center or center-left. Then they can argue for their vision,” Khanna said. “And then it’s for the American people and the primary to decide.” A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. articles.body: Former President Joe Biden would not have run for reelection in 2024 if he had known about his cancer, he said in an interview released Wednesday in which he also sought to downplay the historic debate performance that helped end his political career. "If I had known that I was feeling lousy because I had cancer, I would have not gone forward because I don't think an 80-year-old man with cancer should be running," he said in the interview with People magazine , which was conducted last week following Democrats’ big midterm wins and ahead of his upcoming memoir’s release. The former president announced his diagnosis — Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer — in May 2025, just four months after leaving the White House. It triggered an outpouring of public support — but it also raised questions about how doctors failed to catch the cancer earlier and whether it might have contributed to Biden’s apparent decline toward the end of his term. “I think it’s very sad, actually. I’m surprised that it wasn’t, you know, the public wasn’t notified a long time ago because to get to [a Gleason score of] 9, that’s a long time,” President Donald Trump told reporters shortly after Biden’s announcement. Prior to his diagnosis, Biden hadn’t been screened for prostate cancer since 2014 . U.S. guidelines have long recommended that men shouldn't be screened for the cancer once they hit their 70s. Biden also downplayed his poor June 2024 debate performance against Trump that contributed to his exit from the Democratic ticket a month later. “To me, it was not very consequential,” he said. “First of all, I thought there would be another debate, which there wasn’t. But notwithstanding the fact that there wasn’t another debate, it didn’t disturb me because it wasn’t consequential.” Biden’s son, Hunter, has said he believes the cancer was responsible for the performance. His weak showing on the debate stage led to mounting calls within his party for him to withdraw, an effort eventually backed by longtime friends and allies such as former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi . The former president’s memoir , “Promise Me, America,” will go on sale next week. Biden wrote Sunday on X that the cancer meant he “won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped.” But he still feels sharp, he told the magazine. “I’m not saying I’ll live forever, but the point is that, you know, I have all my faculties, I have access to all the things I had before and, you know, I feel good,” he said.
articles.headline: Biden says he wouldn't have run in 2024 if he knew about his cancer

articles.body: When Annie Andrews announced her longshot campaign for U.S. Senate last May, the Democrat from South Carolina pitched herself as a “busy mom.” “Lindsey [Graham] is going to tell you I am radical, that I am crazy,” Andrews said in her launch video . “But here’s the thing: I am literally a busy mom and a pediatrician who plays peek-a-boo with my patients, watches Bluey with my kids … and spends most of my free time shuttling them to dance, Tae Kwon Do and football.” Now, she is one of a record number of women who will serve in the next Congress. And as a 46-year-old mother of three school-aged children, she’s among several Democratic women who flipped seats and governor’s mansions this November with campaign messages centered on parenting and affordability. It’s a notable campaign shift from previous election cycles: This year, female candidates focused less on the historic nature of their bids, or culture war issues that have long fomented divisions over gender and electability. Instead, they zeroed in on an economic message emphasizing bread-and-butter concerns — like how rising costs were squeezing families, including theirs. “Moms understand kitchen table issues better than perhaps anyone,” said Jessica Mackler, president of EMILY’s List, the group that recruits and backs female Democratic candidates who support abortion rights. “They understand how to stretch a paycheck. They understand what it is like to walk through a grocery store and have to put something back on the shelf.” Senate, House and gubernatorial campaigns spent a combined $72 million on ads featuring the words “mom” or “mother” in 2026, according to AdImpact — a 50% increase from the $48 million spent in 2024 and double the spending on these kind of ads from 2022. In many races, Democrats leaned on their experiences as parents to dismiss the kind of culture war attacks that have been effective for Republicans in recent years. “They want to run an entire campaign saying that I’m too woke … I plan to spend an entire campaign focused on the fact that working people are too broke,” Democratic Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa said in one of her final TV ads . “My pronouns are mom, Texan and soon-to-be governor.” Campaign messaging around gender and representation can be fraught: In 2016, Hillary Clinton’s “I’m With Her” campaign slogan fell short as she failed in her pledge to break the “highest, hardest glass ceiling.” In 2024, Kamala Harris’ campaign was decidedly less overt in its messaging about the barrier-breaking potential of her candidacy. But debates about gender seemed inescapable as Trump called her “weak” and then-Sen. JD Vance said the Democratic Party was run by “childless cat ladies.” This cycle was different. In a 2026 environment driven by concerns about affordability and the cost of living, Democratic operatives said it was an easy decision for women and mothers in particular to lean on their home lives to connect with voters. At least 159 women will serve in the 120th Congress, according to the Center for American Women and Politics, with Democratic women outnumbering Republicans by roughly five-to-one. Many of the newly elected Democrats are younger moms. Their victories, especially in battleground districts and states long seen as Republican strongholds, have emboldened Democratic groups dedicated to electing more women, who argue the candidates offer a blueprint for winning races going forward. Veteran Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said her party’s female candidates “really got points for having the right priorities and being in touch with real people's lives." "It used to be that women with young children just didn't run, and we were electing all these women who had grown children or no children, and then we were electing women with young children, but they were hiding them, if you will,” Lake said. “Now [candidates] were bringing them out as major credentialers, and that has been changing over time." Winning Democratic candidates told POLITICO they did not hesitate to talk about their families and personal experiences on the trail. “I didn’t need anyone giving me talking points on how expensive groceries are,” said Representative-elect Teresa Benitez-Thompson, who won a heavily Republican House district in northern Nevada. “I don’t need anyone telling me how expensive gas is because I am filling up my tank … running kids all around town.” JoAnna Mendoza, a single mom who flipped a swing district in the Tucson, Arizona, suburbs – said she spent the night before the election in the emergency room with her 10-year-old son. “That is what parents face. That is what moms go through. Their kids are sick, they have to take time off of work, or they have to leave work,” Mendoza said. “It is important for people to see themselves in their elected leaders.” Uncomfortable questions surrounding gender and electability nevertheless persist in the run-up to the next presidential election. Some in the Democratic Party at least privately question whether they should nominate another woman at the top of the ticket in 2028. “My message to people who would say that is: cut it out,” said Mackler. “This election clearly demonstrates that women are the drivers of Democrats' path to power, and we should embrace their leadership at all levels of the ballot.” Lake, the Democratic pollster, said the surge in female Democratic victors showed how fed up voters are with the status quo, calling it a “Hail Mary for change.” “It is so bad, it is so failed, we're going to elect these women who will hold people accountable,” she said, adding that voters, particularly women, “were really upset with how out of touch the older white men seemed with their families' lives” after a decade of Trump and Joe Biden running the country. Democratic candidates do not have a monopoly on talking about family life. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the Republican governor of Arkansas, sailed to reelection last week with a campaign that highlighted her three children and efforts to cut grocery taxes and bring down the cost of living for other families. Messages around motherhood also featured prominently at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, earlier this year. The messaging is part of a broader shift in the public conversation, said Abby McCloskey, a conservative policy analyst. “For a long time, to be taken seriously in politics, your professional side went first and your personal side went far after, and that was especially the case for women,” she said. “I think there's been broader cultural shifts that, and probably in a desire for authenticity and connection, why that is no longer necessarily the case.”Democratic campaign veterans said the renewed focus on motherhood gave their candidates an edge as they try to counter swing voters’ deep-seated biases against female candidates. One Democratic pollster, granted anonymity to speak candidly about voters’ biases, said voters still have “bad reactions” to women running for office who are perceived as “cold.” Talking about motherhood and family life, the pollster said, allowed candidates to come across as warm while pushing back against the idea that their candidates are too radical or left-wing. “In some of these places where you have to win over a bunch of conservative folks, the candidate can come across as just a regular mom,” the pollster said. “Not a scary, left, woke lady.” The beginning of Jocelyn Benson’s campaign launch video showed the Democrat hugging her son in their family’s kitchen. Now Michigan’s Democratic governor-elect, Benson told POLITICO she was “very intentional” about inviting kids to join her on stage during her celebration on Election Night. “I think leaders in this moment, and I think parents, moms in particular, recognize this as an opportunity to show a different way of leading and of being a good person and a good citizen,” she said.

articles.body: <p>La política económica es una disciplina narrativa, y unas elecciones generales suelen traer giros de guión, más aún si las encuestas apuntan a un cambio de Gobierno. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-09/el-pp-ampliara-hasta-los-50-anos-de-edad-el-aval-publico-para-pagar-la-entrada-de-una-casa.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-09/el-pp-ampliara-hasta-los-50-anos-de-edad-el-aval-publico-para-pagar-la-entrada-de-una-casa.html">El programa económico del PP</a> propone, básicamente, rebajas de impuestos, un aumento de gasto y el endurecimiento de la política migratoria en un contexto de cierta fatiga de la economía española, agravada por la incertidumbre geopolítica. <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-30/espana-crecio-en-el-tercer-trimestre-un-27.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-30/espana-crecio-en-el-tercer-trimestre-un-27.html">El PIB crece hoy cerca del 3%</a>, tres veces más que la media europea, y el empleo está en máximos, pero hay malestar por la vivienda y el deterioro del poder adquisitivo, y el ciclo económico va camino de agotarse. articles.body: <p>Parapetados bajo el puente de Triana, en el recodo con el Paseo de La O, y haciendo frente a un par de intensos chaparrones. Así ha arrancado <a href="https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/adelante-andalucia-se-presentara-en-solitario-a-las-generales-recogemos-el-legado-de-las-ultimas-elecciones-andaluzas.html&ved=2ahUKEwiGlpzSrIOYAxXLgP0HHasVBYAQFnoECBoQAQ&usg=AOvVaw1RQkiQEfdS9owT0X8n_wM1" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/adelante-andalucia-se-presentara-en-solitario-a-las-generales-recogemos-el-legado-de-las-ultimas-elecciones-andaluzas.html&ved=2ahUKEwiGlpzSrIOYAxXLgP0HHasVBYAQFnoECBoQAQ&usg=AOvVaw1RQkiQEfdS9owT0X8n_wM1">su primera campaña para unas elecciones generales Adelante Andalucía</a>. articles.body: <p>Podemos ha elegido el madrileño Espacio Rastro para cerrar la precampaña electoral para las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre. articles.body: El 3 de novembre, el BOE va publicar les llistes definitives de cada candidatura a les eleccions generals del 29 de novembre. A la circumscripció de Barcelona , els partits hi han inclòs un bon grapat de cares conegudes de la política municipal . Els plats forts són Ada Colau i Jordi Hereu , exalcaldes de Barcelona i caps de llista del PSC i de Front Ampli a la província. Un altre cap de llista que prové del municipalisme és el del PP, l’alcalde de Badalona Xavier García Albiol . Tot i això, dins les candidatures dels partits hi ha més noms familiars. Jordi Hereu (PSC) Alcalde de Barcelona entre el 2006 i el 2011, és el cap de llista socialista a Barcelona. Després d’anys fora de la primera línia política, Pedro Sánchez el va rescatar com a ministre d’Indústria i Turisme el 2023. Ada Colau (Front Ampli) Alcaldessa entre el 2015 i el 2023 i ara cap de llista del Front Ampli a Barcelona. A més, és un cas peculiar, perquè és la candidata a la presidència del govern de la coalició. Això no acostuma a passar, normalment el presidenciable és el cap de llista de Madrid , com passa amb Sánchez, Feijoo i Abascal. Xavier García Albiol (PP) Alcalde de Badalona a dia d’avui. Un dels principals actius dels Partit Popular a Catalunya. Tot i això, ja ha deixat clar que no pensa deixar el càrrec al capdavant del consistori badaloní i el PP hauria de fer una excepció als seus estatuts interns perquè pugui compaginar els càrrecs. Gabriel Colomé (PSC) Repeteix a les llistes del PSC al senat . Hi va com a número 2 i en l’última legislatura ja ha estat senador a Madrid. A Barcelona, Colomé va ser regidor socialista a l’oposició durant el mandat de Xavier Trias. Lucía Martín (Front Ampli) Amb poques opcions de ser escollida, però la que va més amunt a les llistes. Regidora des del 2019 i que, en el segon mandat d’Ada Colau com a alcaldessa va ser, a més, la regidora d’Habitatge i del districte de Sant Andreu. Gerardo Pisarello (Front Ampli) Primer tinent d’alcaldia d’Ada Colau del 2015 al 2019 i regidor de Sarrià-Sant Gervasi . A més, serà l’alcaldable dels Comuns per a les eleccions municipals del mes de maig. Joan Subirats (Front Ampli) Regidor, com Lucía Martín, el segon mandat de Colau. Només hi va ser dos anys, fins que Pedro Sánchez el va nomenar ministre d’Universitats del govern de coalició, càrrec que va ocupar del 2021 al 2023. Juan Milián (PP) Els populars també tenen regidors barcelonins a les seves files. Milián va ser al consistori entre el 2023 i el 2025, fins que va ser nomenat com a senador . Ara, però, és el número 3 dels populars per al Congrés dels Diputats . Víctor Martí (PP) Actualment, encara és regidor del Partit Popular a l’Ajuntament de Barcelona. A diferència de Milián, el seu lloc 23 a la candidatura del PP és més aviat simbòlic i sense opció de ser diputat . Mercedes Vidal (ERC) És la número 2 d’Esquerra al Senat . Tot i això, prové de l’òrbita dels Comuns i va ser regidora de Mobilitat i del districte d’ Horta-Guinardó durant el primer mandat d’Ada Colau a l’Ajuntament (2015-2019) . articles.body: Sense ascensor durant dues setmanes i la situació va per llarg . Els veïns de l’edifici del número 112 del carrer d’Andrade s’han posat en contacte amb l ‘Infobarris perquè no tenen ascensor des del 29 d’octubre. Una inspecció de la Generalitat de Catalunya va determinar que no podia seguir en funcionament perquè no era prou segur . Els veïns amb problemes de mobilitat s’han quedat aïllats a casa i la comunitat de veïns està indignada perquè fa quatre anys que batallen i paguen una derrama per millorar l’ascensor. Segons diuen, però, la deixadesa del seu administrador de finques i l’empresa d’ascensors els han portat a aquesta situació. Persones grans aïllades La Isabel Martínez té gairebé 86 anys i viu a l’onzena planta de l’edifici. “Abans baixava una estona de tant en tant, però ara no puc sortir gens . Com he de sortir sense ascensor? Cada dia estic pitjor d’estar aquí asseguda tot el dia “, explica. El mateix els passa als avis de l’Ariadna Roca. “Hi ha molta gent gran que viu a l’edifici i no poden sortir de casa perquè no poden baixar les escales. Llavors ens hem d’encarregar entre tots els veïns de baixar-los la brossa i anar a fer-los la compra “, lamenta. La Isabel viu a l’onzena planta de l’edifici Quatre anys de gestions i despropòsits per l’ascensor La indignació és màxima entre els veïns d’aquest edifici del carrer d’Andrade perquè fa quatre anys que paguen una derrama i batallen perquè el seu administrador TDB finques , i l’ empresa d’ascensors Fain , facin les obres per fer arribar l’ ascensor a cota zero . Per arreglar aquest tema, la comunitat de veïns es va posar mans a l’obra l’octubre del 2022 i el projecte es va aturar per una baixa laboral. Després es van canviar el pressupost diverses vegades i finalment es va aprovar , però sense arribar a iniciar-se l’obra . Els veïns denuncien que fins i tot van perdre una subvenció que els havien adjudicat perquè l’empresa d’ascensors no va renovar-la dins el termini. El Gerard ha de pujar fins a la vuitena planta i té dos nens petits i dos gossos Els veïns han posat aigua en alguns punts de l’escala pels qui pugen a peu Una de les cadires col·locades a les escales per poder descansar La inspecció de l’ECA l’ha clausurat El temps ha anat passant i, en comptes d’arribar l’execució de l’obra, ha arribat la inspecció de la Generalitat , que va fer uns requeriments per millorar la seguretat . “L’ECA va venir per fer la revisió de l’ascensor que fa cada quatre anys, va trobar unes avaries i aquesta gent tenien sis mesos per fer-ho i no ho van fer . I ara què ens trobem? Ha vingut la Generalitat i ha clausurat l’ascensor”, explica indignada Maria Mercè Yuba, que ha de pujar i baixar les escales amb una fissura al peroné. Els veïns demanen celeritat amb les obres La presidenta de la comunitat, Pepita Cañisá, té les idees clares: “Demano a l’empresa Fain, però també a TDB Finqueses que es posi les piles i que iniciïn les obres ja d’una vegada . La gent no s’ha pogut preparar i estem desesperats “. Al Gerard Compte, veí de la vuitena planta, el preocupa una altra cosa: “El problema no és que comencin o no, el problema és quant temps es passaran amb les obres . Si s’hi involucren al 100 %, es pot fer en un mes, si no, sis mesos passaran”, conclou preocupat. Fain diu que començarà les obres aquesta setmana L’empresa d’ascensors Fain ha explicat a betevé i també als veïns que té previst iniciar les obres de l’ascensor aquesta setmana , amb l’objectiu de reduir al màxim possible el temps sense servei. Quant a una possible solució provisional, expliquen que han valorat la instal·lació d’una cadira puja escales, però les característiques de l’edifici requereixen una fabricació a mida que tardaria aproximadament 12 setmanes i això no permetria donar una resposta immediata a la situació actual. De moment , després de la denúncia de l’ Infobarris , han col·locat el cartell d’inici d’obres . 45.000 ascensors a Barcelona A Barcelona hi ha 45.000 ascensors i, segons, el Col·legi d’Enginyers Industrials de Catalunya tres de cada quatre tenen una antiguitat de més de 30 anys . La normativa obliga a fer revisions cada quatre anys a les finques de més de 20 habitatges, una problemàtica que segons Jordi Sarrats, president del Gremi Empresarial d’Ascensors de Catalunya ha accelerat el dèficit d’operaris del sector , un fet que el gremi ja ha traslladat a les administracions. articles.body: (ACN) L’Hospital Sant Joan de Déu ha implantat un nou model d’atenció als infants amb diabetis en què s’utilitzen dispositius per monitorar la glucosa i alliberar la insulina de forma automatitzada . Amb aquest sistema, únic a Espanya en l’àmbit pediàtric, els pacients poden ser atesos a distància i s’han reduït més d’un 60 % les visites presencials en consultes externes. A més, els ingressos hospitalaris per descompensacions han disminuït en un 80 % i també s’han triplicat els pacients que assoleixen els objectius recomanats de control glucèmic. El cap de la Unitat de Diabetis de l’Hospital Sant Joan de Déu, Roque Cardona , ha destacat que aquest model permet estalviar desplaçaments i espaiar més les consultes. També et pot interessar Reduir l’estrès infantil durant una ressonància és possible a través d’una experiència audiovisual Jordi Escofet 2 minuts de lectura Una o dues visites l’any Amb aquest sistema, aproximadament el 55 % dels pacients només han d’anar a l’hospital una o dues vegades l’any . Així també es poden optimitzar i redistribuir els recursos disponibles, a més de comprar més dispositius d’alliberament automatitzat d’insulina i fer-los extensius a més pacients de l’hospital. De fet, el nombre s’ha duplicat i més de 250 persones tenen accés a aquest sistema. A més, l’any 2019 es van ingressar 12 persones per descompensacions per cetoacidosi i el 2025, només dues, un 80 % menys. “El nou model està basat en el valor, entenent per valor la relació entre la qualitat de les cures que es presten i el cost que suposen” , ha explicat Cardona. Un sistema format amb dues plataformes El sistema està format per dues plataformes: una de vinculada a la història clínica del pacient i amb alertes per a l’equip mèdic i una altra que està coordinada amb un infermer que s’encarrega del triatge . El pacient també disposa d’una aplicació per facilitar informació en temps real dels seus marcadors i de recomanacions d’ajust de pauta. D’aquesta manera, la plataforma analitza diàriament les dades i presta a l’infermer la llista de pacients que requereixen atenció immediata. L’Hospital Sant Joan de Déu és el centre que controla més pacients pediàtrics amb diabetis tipus 1 d’Espanya i aproximadament el 50 % dels infants amb aquesta malaltia residents a Catalunya. En total, registra un centenar de debuts cada any. El centre ha pogut fer realitat aquesta iniciativa gràcies a una convocatòria de compra pública innovadora finançada amb fons europeus FEDER i amb la intervenció del CatSalut i AQuAS. articles.body: La barcelonina Iolanda Batallé ha estat guardonada amb el VIII Premi Proa de Novel·la per la seva obra Lluny de Califòrnia . La novel·la és una història sobre l’amor, la llibertat i la culpa sobre el que es guanya i el que es perd quan es tria una vida però se’n renuncia totes les altres. Lluny de Califòrnia sortirà a la venda el 18 de novembre. La història està protagonitzada per una escriptora , la Maria Viladoms, que als 50 anys retorna a la joventut per enfrontar-se a la noia que va ser. Una decisió empesa per la seva editora, la Maria, amb qui té un estira-i-arronsa durant tota la novel·la. La protagonista de jove poc després de casar-se amb el seu marit, el Joe, marxa becada a la Universitat de Berkeley. Allà coneix el Max, un noi de 19 anys amb qui viu una passió inesperada . La Maria haurà de triar entre el marit que estima , les oportunitats que se li obren i un amor que li capgira la vida . Però aviat descobrirà un costat vulnerable del Max que farà la relació cada vegada més difícil. Des de fa cinc anys dirigeix l’espai cultural i llibreria Ona. És fundadora de l’editorial Rata_ i ha dirigit l’Institut Ramon Llull. Ha escrit novel·la, contes i assaig. articles.body: El Barça ha perdut els primers punts en aquesta edició de la Champions . Les blaugrana han empatat a un davant l’Arsenal . Les angleses s’han avançat a la primera part i Graham Hansen ha empatat a la segona. La falta d’efectivitat ha passat factura a les jugadores de Pere Romeu. Després de l’empat el Barça és colíder empatat a 10 punts amb l’Olympique de Lió . L’Arsenal s’avança al Camp Nou El partit ha començat amb una doble ocasió per a l’Arsenal, però primer Cata Coll i després la rematada al pal d ‘Alessia Russo han fet que el marcador no es mogués. A partir d’aquí les de Pere Romeu han començat dominant i han tingut diverses ocasions clares de gol, però a vegades la falta de punteria i d’altres la portera de l’Arsenal, Misa , o fins i tot la defensa de les angleses han evitat el gol blaugrana. I el que són les coses en un ràpid contraatac les britàniques s’han avançat. Ha estat Maanum al minut 22 qui ha signat el 0 a 1. El Barça ha reaccionat i ha tornat a disposar de diverses ocasions. Paredes, Guijarro, Sydney, Pina i Graham al pal han tingut l’empat a prop, però aquest no ha arribat. El Barça només pot empatar A la segona part el Barça ha seguit dominant i la insistència ha tingut el premi del gol en el minut 59, quan Graham Hansen ha fet l’empat a 1. Les blaugrana han seguit buscant el gol de la victòria, però la manca d’efectivitat ha passat factura a l’equip de Pere Romeu . A més, en els últims minuts l’Arsenal amb la moral de veure l’empat al marcador s’ha estirat una mica i s’ha apropat a la porteria de Cata Coll. Les blaugrana han tingut un últim córner per capgirar el marcador, però aquest ja no s’ha mogut de l’1 a 1.

articles.body: Els serveis municipals han treballat tota la nit i ho segueixen fent durant la jornada de dijous per recuperar la normalitat al centre de Barcelona després d’una nova nit d’aldarulls . Per netejar els carrers, recollir la brossa, recol·locar contenidors i acabar de retirar les restes d’algunes barricades s’hi han hagut de destinar prop de 2.900 persones dels serveis de neteja i recollida de residus. Més enllà de la cinquantena de detinguts, el balanç de la nit pel que fa a altres actuacions ha estat de 42 sortides dels Bombers de Barcelona . La majoria de les actuacions es van dur a terme als entorns de la plaça de Catalunya, el passeig de Gràcia i el carrer de Pelai. D’altra banda, el gruix de desperfectes al mobiliari urbà està vinculat a la crema de 110 contenidors , que ha tingut un cost d’uns 150.000 euros. Des d’aquest dijous, ja s’han començat a substituir i està previst que estiguin tots reposats el proper diumenge, dia 15. A més, es van registrar desperfectes en una desena de comerços.
